entities.summary:
Mahathammaracha I, born as Li Thai, was the first Buddhist philosopher to write in the Thai language. He reigned as King of Sukhothai from roughly 1347 until his death in 1368.

Mahathammaracha I played a significant role in the development of Thai Buddhism, which became a major force in the region. His writings had a lasting impact on the culture and spirituality of the Thai people.

The legacy of Mahathammaracha I can be seen in the many temples and monuments built during his reign, including the famous Wat Phra Kaew in Ayutthaya. His influence extended beyond Thailand, as Buddhist ideas and practices spread throughout Southeast Asia and beyond.

As a testament to his enduring legacy, the story of Mahathammaracha I continues to be celebrated in Thai folklore and literature, inspiring new generations of scholars and enthusiasts alike.
